fix(operators): reject ManagedProvider entries with the same name

## Summary
Reject entries with duplicate names and provide an error message.

Simplified example:
```yaml
kind: ManagedProvider
spec:
  runtimeDeployments:
    - flux:
        registry: ghcr.io/platform-mesh/helm-charts
        chart: example-httpbin-operator
        version: 0.5.14
        values: {replicaCount: 1}
    - flux:
        registry: ghcr.io/platform-mesh/helm-charts
        chart: example-httpbin-operator
        version: 0.5.14
        values: {replicaCount: 3}
```

## What Type of PR Is This?

bug

## Release Notes

```release-note
fix(operators): reject ManagedProvider entries with the same name
```

fix(client-tools): the execution-facts store keeps a 2 GiB byte budget (#4537)

## Summary

Closes #4537. The client's shared warm cache, `.state/client-warm-cache`, reached 14.8 GB on the PC, nearly all of it 46,479 `execution-facts` entries.

`tools/execution-facts.mjs` pruned only entries unused for 7 days, and a hit never refreshed an entry's time. With several worktrees running gates, a week of edits outgrew any reasonable bound: one full set for the 920 client sources is about 300 MB.

The fix is in `tools/execution-facts.mjs`:
- **Byte budget:** `pruneStore` keeps the age rule, then evicts the least recently used entries until the store fits `MAX_STORE_BYTES` (2 GiB, six or seven full sets). This run's entries are never evicted.
- **Last use:** `readStored` refreshes an entry's time on a hit, so the rules evict by last use. An entry every run reads is the last to go.

This store is a cache, never an input: a miss only re-extracts, and every failure warns.

## Tests

- New: `the store evicts the least recently used entries past its byte budget` (in `tests/architecture/execution-facts.test.mjs`). Five 100-byte entries with a 300-byte budget: this run's oldest entry stays, the two least recently used others go. It fails with the eviction loop disabled.
- `node --test tests/architecture/execution.test.mjs tests/architecture/execution-facts.test.mjs`: 18 pass.
- `check:format` passes.

## Native claims

None: a development tool's cache.

## Old tab

Old-tab: safe - tooling only.

## Open items

None.

## Summary

This test-only change makes the rollback setup take the same `helpers.KnownGap(..., helpers.MethodSecretsRotate, err)` path before its `require.NoError`. The `RequireCLIRefusal` check is kept, and the `return` ends only the rollback group.

fix(sdn): policy ACL matches carry the dl_type and nw_proto prerequisites OVS requires (main fix) (#2437)

## Summary
Main 458f48b5b is red on Integration shard 2 (`TestPolicyEngineIntegration/FlowInstallationOnPolicyApplication`, `TestPolicyEngineWithCertificate/AuthenticateWithCertificate`): OVS refuses the policy ACL flows with `bad match: bad prereq`. `RuleGenerator.buildMatch` emitted `nw_proto` and `tp_dst` without `dl_type`, and `tp_*` without `nw_proto`. Since #2360 surfaced the switch error, those flows fail visibly; before it they were silently never installed.

`buildMatch` now adds the OpenFlow prerequisites when the match does not set them:
- `dl_type=0x86dd` for IPv6 address fields; `dl_type=0x0800` for IPv4 address fields, an IP protocol, or a TCP/UDP port
- `nw_proto=6` for TCP ports and `nw_proto=17` for UDP ports when no IP protocol is set
- an explicit `EthType` or `IPProto` is never overridden

## Tests
- Test first: `TestRuleGenerator_BuildMatchPrerequisites` (commit 8265a5242 fails alone, passes with 0e2a16e63)
- `go vet` and `go test ./pkg/sdn/policy/` pass; `go vet -tags integration ./test/integration/sdn/` is clean; Integration shard 2 in this PR's CI is the proof

## Review note (sensitive path: network access enforcement)
A match on a port or IP protocol alone, with no address fields, now defaults to IPv4 (`dl_type=0x0800`). So a port-only DENY rule matches IPv4 traffic only, not IPv6. Before this change such a flow was refused by the switch and nothing was installed, so this is not a regression; the reviewer should say whether a port-only rule must install an IPv6 twin flow.

Refs #2437

fix(ntp): no NTP REST routes on a node without an NTP backend (main fix) (#2435)

## Why main is red

Main run 45694677196 at 458f48b5b failed Web Console E2E in `web/e2e/real-server/ntp.spec.ts`. The real-server daemon has no `ntp:` config, yet:

- `daemon.go` always builds the NTP gRPC service; with no config its backend is nil.
- `serve.go` passed that service to the REST registry whenever it was non-nil, so `ntpRoutes()` registered the NTP routes.
- The capabilities list therefore reported `GET /api/v1/ntp/status` enabled, and the spec expected 200. The route answered 503, because `requireBackend` returns Unavailable when there is no backend.

This is a real failure, not a flake. It arrived with #2159 (the NTP page behind the capability gate) and is tracked in #2435.

## Fix

- `NTPGRPCService.Configured()` reports whether the service has a backend.
- `serve.go` hands the REST registry the NTP service only when `svc != nil && svc.Configured()`. An unconfigured node then offers no NTP REST operations, and the console shows its not-enabled card. A configured node behaves as before, and gRPC registration is unchanged.

## Main-fix lane mfntp2435a (DS-10622)

The test commit comes first: `TestNTPGRPCService_Configured` failed to build before the fix. Results:

- go vet on the touched packages is clean.
- `go build ./cmd/...` passes.
- The REST NTP and capability tests pass.
- Playwright `--list` shows all 62 real-server tests.

Two failures already exist on main and are not touched here:
- `pkg/api/daemon` `TestWithQUICNTPServiceOptionWiresTheBackend`, which fails at 458f48b5b too;
- the QUIC not-configured subtests, which fail with "no codec available".

Refs #2435

fix(shell): unset stale env keys in fish with set -e

Closes #3926

<!-- claude-code-review:summary -->

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Medium Risk**
>
> The change touches the shared fish shell hook template used by every fish user on each prompt, but the edit is narrowly scoped and backed by new integration coverage across all supported shells.
>
> **Overview**
>
> This PR fixes a bug where `windsor env --hook` output in fish never actually unset stale environment variables, because fish has no bare `unset` builtin. The fish hook template now pipes hook output through `string replace -r '^unset ' 'set -e '` before evaluation, rewriting POSIX-style `unset` lines into fish's `set -e` syntax. The PR also replaces the old single-assertion `hook_test.go` integration test with a much more thorough `shell_env_test.go` that drives real bash, zsh, fish, tcsh, and PowerShell sessions through hook and eval paths, checking value fidelity, idempotent reloads, and that context-switch unsets actually take effect — with a `knownBugs` registry that tracks still-open quoting issues per shell so fixes can't silently regress.
>
> A new `shell-env` CI matrix job runs these tests on ubuntu, macOS, and Windows with the real shell binaries installed, so the fish fix (and the other shells) are now exercised directly in CI rather than only via unit tests on the template string.

<!-- /claude-code-review:summary -->
